decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
response.rationale: Classic pancreatitis-type pain plus markedly elevated lipase satisfy acute pancreatitis criteria; CT can be normal in early/mild acute pancreatitis, so the negative pancreatic finding does not override the biochemical evidence.

rejected.why: Epigastric pain and PPI nonresponse are nonspecific, and peptic ulcer disease does not explain the markedly elevated lipase.
No previous similar pain and no acute pancreatic abnormality on CT do not support chronic pancreatitis.
Hyperglycemia and diabetes history are present, but there is no ketosis/acidosis data and DKA does not explain the lipase elevation.
Decreased oral intake and diabetes are nonspecific and do not indicate pancreatic insufficiency.
Known CKD and elevated creatinine are chronic findings and do not explain the acute epigastric pain and elevated lipase.
